featR: A Unified Toolkit for Feature Selection

Source: R/featR-package.R
featR-package.Rd

featR gathers filter, regularization, wrapper, and dimensionality-reduction methods for choosing predictors and puts them behind one calling convention and one return type, so that trying a different method is a one-word change rather than a rewrite. Each method is a single function call on a data frame; there is no pipeline object to build first.

Details

Calling convention. Selection functions are called as fs_<method>(data, target, ...). data holds the observations (a data.frame, or a data.table or matrix where the method accepts one) and target is the name of the outcome column inside data, never a separate vector. Method-specific options follow, and housekeeping arguments (seed, verbose, n_cores) come last wherever a method supports them. The functions with no outcome to name take no target: fs_unsupervised and fs_correlation score features without one, and fs_pca and fs_svd decompose a numeric table.

Return value. Every selection function returns an object of class fs_result, a list with the elements:

  • selected: character vector of the chosen feature names (possibly empty).

  • scores: per-feature scores, usually a named numeric vector covering every candidate feature (a data.frame for a few methods), or NULL when the method produces no comparable per-feature score.

  • method: single string naming what actually ran, for example "supervised_correlation", "lasso", or "svm_linear".

  • task: "classification", "regression", or NA when the method has no task.

  • model: the fitted model when the method fits one, otherwise NULL.

  • details: named list of method-specific extras, documented per function.

  • call: the matched call.

Results have print() and summary() methods, and selected extracts the chosen names. fs_pca and fs_svd are dimensionality reduction rather than selection, so they are the two exceptions: each returns its own plain list, documented on its own help page.

Dependencies. Only data.table, parallel, stats, utils, and withr are hard dependencies. Every modeling engine (caret, glmnet, kernlab, randomForest, Boruta, earth, MASS, brms, RSpectra, and the rest) is a suggested package, loaded only on the code path that needs it and checked at the point of use: if one is missing you get an error naming the packages and the exact install.packages() call to run, rather than a cryptic failure deep in a model fit.

Reproducibility and resources. featR never seeds the RNG on its own. Functions that use randomness take seed = NULL; supplying a seed sets it for that call only and restores the caller's RNG state on exit. Every function is sequential by default, parallelism is opt-in through n_cores (or parallel = TRUE), worker requests are capped at the detected core count, and any cluster featR starts is stopped when the call returns.

Available methods.

Filters

No model is fitted, so they are cheap and scale to wide data. fs_supervised (absolute Pearson correlation or one-way ANOVA F against the target), fs_unsupervised (variance, MAD, IQR, range, missingness, distinct values), fs_chi (chi-squared tests for categorical features), fs_infogain (information gain and gain ratio), and fs_correlation (drops redundant members of highly correlated groups).

Regularization and embedded importance

One model fit whose own structure names the survivors. fs_lasso (L1 penalty), fs_elastic (L1/L2 mixture), fs_randomforest (permutation importance with held-out evaluation), and fs_mars (the predictors an earth model retains).

Wrappers

A model is refitted over candidate subsets: the most expensive family, and the most closely tailored to the model you intend to use. fs_recursivefeature (caret recursive feature elimination), fs_svm (SVM-RFE, or random-forest screening, plus a tuned SVM), fs_boruta (all-relevant selection against shadow features), fs_stepwise (AIC stepwise regression), and fs_bayes (brms models compared with loo).

Dimensionality reduction

New components replace the original columns instead of a subset being kept. fs_pca (principal components with tidy output and an optional plot) and fs_svd (truncated singular value decomposition with an optional approximate solver).
